chapters: Qualified Identity, Process, Boundaries, and Infinity
focus:
Qualified Identity, Process, Boundaries, and Infinity
At noon, a cloud hangs above the lake. At 12:05 it has moved, expanded, lost water, gained water, split at one edge, and merged with vapour at another. A child points and says,
“That cloud is getting darker.”
The sentence presupposes that the subject persists through change. Without that presupposition, there is no it to get darker. Yet no sharp boundary tells us which droplets compose the cloud, and no material core remains fixed.

Conclusion
Natural language is the main medium in which scientific questions, explanations, disagreements, and institutional decisions are expressed. Its economy leaves source, identity, scope, coverage, authority, time, and alternative interpretations implicit when context is sufficient for human readers. Computational use requires those variables to become explicit at the points where they change denotation, inference, or action.
